blocks.text: FIELD GUIDE FG-07 · 2ND EDITION
The Spares Cataloguer's Field Guide
How to write MRO spares and consumables data so that everyone finds the same part.
Inside
• 8 golden rules you can learn over a coffee
• 10 chapters: bearings, seals, O-rings, belts, oils, greases, filters, bolts, hoses and gloves
• Before / after examples for every field
• FAQ, checklist and lookup tables
Published by the Materials Cataloguing Team · October 2026 · Sample document for system testing
Hi, cataloguer!
You're the person who decides whether the warehouse holds one bin of 6205-2RS/C3 bearings or five bins of the same bearing under five different names. This guide is here to make that decision easy.

Each record you work on arrives as rows with three columns: Item, Attribute and Value. In this guide we call the item a category (what kind of thing it is) and the attribute a field (one fact about it). You'll translate each row into the guide's words and write it back in the same three columns, in the same order. If your tool has a fourth column for notes, list the rule codes you used - for example GR2; BRG-1.

rows.Use it when: You see inches, psi, gallons, pounds

rows.What you'll find: One per category: fields at a glance, rule cards, before/after
The questions everyone asks in week one
AS568 sizes, dash sizes, UNC threads, V-belt offsets
rows.Use it when: A rule card tells you to look something up

rows.Meaning: The kind of item, e.g. Rolling Bearing. Written in the Item column, Title Case.
One fact about the item, e.g. bore_diameter. Written in the Attribute column as a lower_snake_case key.
The fact itself, e.g. 25 mm. Written in the Value column.
A closed list of allowed values. If a field has one, the value must come from it.
A small box in each chapter telling you, in IF / THEN form, how to turn messy input into a clean value.
Your two safety valves: TBD when the value is missing, CHECK: when it can't be mapped.

blocks.text: The order of work. 1) Tidy spaces. 2) Missing? write TBD. 3) Fix the category (GR1). 4) Fix the field key (GR2). 5) Apply the chapter's rule card. 6) Convert units (GR5) and tidy numbers (GR4). 7) Still doesn't fit? CHECK: (GR7).
The 8 golden rules
Learn these and you'll get 80 % of rows right without opening a chapter.
GR1 Use the category name from this guide

Every row starts with a category. Write it exactly as the chapter title, in Title Case: Rolling Bearing, O-Ring, Hex Bolt. Nicknames like Brg, Oring or Hyd Hose are fine to receive - just never to write.
GR2 Field keys are lower_snake_case

The attribute column holds a field key, not a label. Keys are lower case with underscores, exactly as listed in each chapter's 'Fields at a glance' table. Labels such as 'Shaft Dia' or 'Pack Size' are translated into the key.
GR3 Picklist values are spelled exactly like the guide
If a field has a picklist, copy the value character for character: words in Title Case, acronyms in capitals, symbols kept (Deep Groove Ball, Lithium Complex, SiC/Carbon, JIC 37° Female Swivel).
GR4 Numbers: metric, one space, short and tidy

Measured values are metric: number, one space, unit (25 mm, 10.3 bar, 208 L). Use at most one decimal and drop trailing zeros (70 mm, not 70.0 mm). The only exception is O-ring dimensions, which always carry two decimals (3.53 mm, 25.00 mm).
GR5 Convert imperial units - don't keep both
Inches, pounds, gallons, psi and ounces are converted with the cheat sheet on page 4. Write only the metric result; never '50.8 mm (2 in)'
GR6 Don't know? Write TBD
Empty cells, dashes, n/a, ?, 'unknown', 'see drawing' all become TBD (capitals). Never guess - a TBD gets fixed, a guess gets bought.
Sample field guide for testing data standardization. Keep it on your desk, not in a drawer.
GR7 Can't map it? Flag it with CHECK:
If a value doesn't fit the field's picklist or format even after every rule in its chapter, write CHECK: followed by a space and the original text. A reviewer will pick it up.
GR8 One row in, one row out

Never split one row into several or merge rows together. Keep the order of the file. If a value carries information for another field (like 'EP2' for a grease), use only the part that belongs to this row's field.
Cheat sheet: units
Multiply, then round as the field says. If the chapter has a standard-pack or lookup table, that wins over the plain conversion.
Rounding. Round half up. 15.876 kg becomes 15.9 kg; 344.7 bar becomes 345 bar when the field asks for whole numbers; 24.9936 mm becomes 24.99 mm for O-rings.
Rolling Bearing

Bearings are the most duplicated items in any spares catalogue, because every manufacturer adds its own suffixes to the same basic part. Your job is to strip the brand dialect and leave a designation any store-person can match on the shelf.
Write the category as: Rolling Bearing  You may receive: Bearing; Ball Bearing; Roller Bearing; Brg; Deep Groove Ball Bearing; Anti-friction Bearing

rows.Labels you may see: Designation; Part No; Bearing No; Bearing Number; Code

blocks.text: Rule cards

BRG-1 designation
IF seal suffix IN (2RS1, 2RSH, 2RSR, LLU, DDU, 2RS) THEN write -2RS
IF seal suffix IN (ZZ, 2ZR, 2Z, ZZC) THEN write -2Z
IF clearance suffix present (C2, C3, C4, C5) THEN append /Cn at the end
REMOVE spaces, dots and extra hyphens between the parts; REMOVE cage codes (M, MA, J, TN9) - they go to cage_material
Watch out! Don't 'upgrade' a bearing: 6205 and 6205-2RS are different parts. Only translate what is written.

BRG-2 bearing_type
IF value IN (DGBB; deep groove; radial ball) THEN write "Deep Groove Ball"
IF value IN (ACBB; angular contact) THEN write "Angular Contact Ball"
IF value IN (CRB; cylindrical) THEN write "Cylindrical Roller"
IF value IN (SRB; spherical; self-aligning roller) THEN write "Spherical Roller"
IF value IN (TRB; taper; tapered) THEN write "Tapered Roller"
IF value IN (thrust) THEN write "Thrust Ball"
IF value IN (self-aligning ball) THEN write "Self-Aligning Ball"

BRG-3 bore_diameter
IF unit is inch THEN multiply by 25.4
IF no unit THEN assume mm (bearing catalogues are metric)

BRG-4 outside_diameter
Same as bore_diameter

BRG-5 width
Same as bore_diameter
BRG-6 seal_type

IF value IN (rubber seals both sides; 2RS1; LLU; sealed both sides) THEN write "2RS"
IF value IN (metal shields; shielded both sides; ZZ) THEN write "2Z"
IF value IN (one rubber seal; RS1) THEN write "RS"
IF value IN (one shield) THEN write "Z"
IF value IN (open; no seals) THEN write "Open"
BRG-7 internal_clearance

IF value IN (C2; less than normal) THEN write "C2"
IF value IN (normal; CN; standard) THEN write "CN"
IF value IN (C3; C 3; greater than normal) THEN write "C3"
IF value IN (C4) THEN write "C4"
IF value IN (C5) THEN write "C5"
BRG-8 cage_material

IF value IN (J; pressed steel; steel) THEN write "Steel"
IF value IN (M; MA; machined brass; brass) THEN write "Brass"
IF value IN (TN9; TN; nylon; PA66; polyamide) THEN write "Polyamide"
Pro tip. Bore code shortcut: for series 6000-6300 with bore code 04 and up, bore = code x 5 mm (6205 -> 25 mm). Use it to sanity-check, not to fill blanks.

Mechanical Seal
Mechanical seals follow API 682, so most of the vocabulary is already standard - it's just written fifteen different ways. Stick to the API words and you're done.
Write the category as: Mechanical Seal  You may receive: Mech Seal; Mechanical Seal; Pump Seal; Cartridge Seal

rows.Labels you may see: Shaft Size; Shaft Dia; Sleeve Size; Shaft
Flush Plan; API Plan; Piping Plan

blocks.text: Rule cards

MSL-1 arrangement
IF value IN (single; single seal) THEN write "Arrangement 1"
IF value IN (tandem; dual unpressurized; dual unpressurised) THEN write "Arrangement 2"
IF value IN (double; dual pressurized; double pressurized; back-to-back) THEN write "Arrangement 3"

MSL-2 seal_category
IF value matches cat 1/2/3 in any spelling (CAT2, Cat. 2) THEN write Category n

MSL-3 seal_type
IF value IN (pusher; O-ring pusher; rotating pusher) THEN write "Type A"
IF value IN (metal bellows; low temperature bellows) THEN write "Type B"
IF value IN (high temperature metal bellows; flexible graphite bellows) THEN write "Type C"

MSL-4 shaft_diameter
REMOVE the diameter sign Ø
IF unit is inch THEN multiply by 25.4

MSL-5 face_combination
IF value IN (carbon; carbon graphite; antimony carbon) THEN write "Carbon"
IF value IN (silicon carbide; SSiC; RBSiC; SiC) THEN write "SiC"
IF value IN (tungsten carbide; WC; TC) THEN write "TC"
Translate each face with the picklist, keep the order given, join with / (no spaces)
Separators vs, v, against, - , / all mean the same
Sample field guide for testing data standardization. Keep it on your desk, not in a drawer.
MSL-6 secondary_seal
IF value IN (nitrile; Buna-N; Buna) THEN write "NBR"
IF value IN (hydrogenated nitrile; HSN) THEN write "HNBR"
IF value IN (Viton; fluorocarbon; FPM) THEN write "FKM"
IF value IN (Kalrez; perfluoroelastomer; perfluoro) THEN write "FFKM"
IF value IN (EPR; ethylene propylene) THEN write "EPDM"
IF value IN (silicone; Si) THEN write "VMQ"
IF value IN (Aflas; TFE/P) THEN write "FEPM"
MSL-7 flush_plan
Write Plan, one space, the plan number, suffix letter in capitals: Plan 53A
Combined plans joined with /: Plan 11/52
CHAPTER 3 · CODE ORG
O-Ring
O-rings are cheap, but a wrong one stops a compressor. The two things that matter are size and compound. Note the special rule: O-ring dimensions always have two decimals.
Write the category as: O-Ring  You may receive: O-ring; Oring; O Ring; Seal Ring; Toroidal Seal

rows.Labels you may see: Size; Dash No; Dash Number; AS568
RGD; AED; Explosive Decompression; ED Resistant

blocks.text: Rule cards

ORG-1 size_reference
IF value is a 3-digit dash number with or without prefix (214, -214, 2-214, AS 568-214) THEN write AS568-214
The leading '2-' used by some suppliers is a compound prefix, not part of the size

ORG-2 inner_diameter
IF inch THEN x 25.4
ALWAYS two decimals: 25.00 mm

ORG-3 cross_section
Decimal comma becomes point: 3,53 -> 3.53 mm

ORG-4 material
IF value IN (nitrile; Buna-N; Buna) THEN write "NBR"
IF value IN (hydrogenated nitrile; HSN) THEN write "HNBR"
IF value IN (Viton; fluorocarbon; FPM) THEN write "FKM"
IF value IN (Kalrez; perfluoroelastomer; perfluoro) THEN write "FFKM"
IF value IN (EPR; ethylene propylene) THEN write "EPDM"
IF value IN (silicone; Si) THEN write "VMQ"
IF value IN (Aflas; TFE/P) THEN write "FEPM"

ORG-5 hardness
IF value in duro, A, Sh A, Shore A or IRHD THEN write {n} Shore A (IRHD treated as equal)

ORG-6 aed_resistant
IF value mentions RGD resistant, AED, ED, NORSOK M-710 or ISO 23936-2 THEN Yes
Pro tip. Two decimals for O-rings is deliberate: AS568 sizes differ by as little as 0.08 mm, and rounding to one decimal merges different rings.
V-Belt
V-belts come in classical (A, B, C, D), narrow wedge (SPZ, SPA, SPB, SPC) and US narrow (3V, 5V, 8V) sections. The section plus the datum length is the whole identity of the belt.
Write the category as: V-Belt  You may receive: V Belt; Vee Belt; Wedge Belt; Drive Belt; Fan Belt
Rule cards

VBT-1 belt_section
IF value IN (13x8; 13 x 8 mm) THEN write "A"
IF value IN (17x11; 17 x 11 mm) THEN write "B"
IF value IN (22x14) THEN write "C"
IF value IN (32x19) THEN write "D"
IF value IN (spz) THEN write "SPZ"
IF value IN (spa) THEN write "SPA"
IF value IN (spb) THEN write "SPB"
IF value IN (spc) THEN write "SPC"
IF value IN (XPZ; cogged SPZ) THEN write "XPZ"
IF value IN (XPA) THEN write "XPA"
IF value IN (XPB) THEN write "XPB"
IF value IN (3V; 9N) THEN write "3V"
IF value IN (5V; 15N) THEN write "5V"

VBT-2 datum_length
REMOVE Ld, Lw, Lp prefixes
IF value looks like A42, B75 (classical, inside length in inches) THEN datum = inches x 25.4 + offset
(A +30, B +40, C +58, D +75 mm)

VBT-3 construction
IF value IN (wrapped; classical wrapped; envelope) THEN write "Wrapped"
IF value IN (cogged; notched; raw edge; XP) THEN write "Raw Edge Cogged"
IF value IN (power band; banded; joined; multi-belt) THEN write "Banded"

VBT-4 matched_set_qty
Keep only the number: set of 4 -> 4

CHAPTER 5 · CODE LUB
Lubricating Oil
One oil, a dozen names. Grade, base stock and application are what make two oils interchangeable - brand names are not part of this guide and never go in a field.
Write the category as: Lubricating Oil  You may receive: Oil; Lube Oil; Lubricant; Turbine Oil; Hydraulic Oil; Gear Oil; Compressor Oil
Rule cards

LUB-1 viscosity_grade
IF value is VG46, ISO 46, ISO VG46 or 46 cSt THEN ISO VG 46 (valid ISO grades: 10 15 22 32 46 68 100 150 220 320 460 680)
IF value is a multigrade like 15W40 THEN SAE 15W-40 (hyphen before the hot grade)
IF value is SAE 90, SAE 140 THEN keep SAE {n}

LUB-2 base_oil
IF value IN (mineral; Group I; Group II) THEN write "Mineral"
IF value IN (Group III; hydrocracked) THEN write "Group III"
IF value IN (synthetic hydrocarbon; polyalphaolefin; PAO) THEN write "PAO"
IF value IN (ester; synthetic ester) THEN write "Ester"
IF value IN (polyglycol; polyalkylene glycol; PAG) THEN write "PAG"
Watch out! 'Semi-synthetic' and 'synthetic blend' don't tell you the base - write CHECK: and let the lubrication engineer decide.
Sample field guide for testing data standardization. Keep it on your desk, not in a drawer.
LUB-3 application
IF value IN (R&O turbine; turbine; steam turbine) THEN write "Turbine"
IF value IN (AW hydraulic; hydraulic; HM) THEN write "Hydraulic"
IF value IN (EP gear; gear; industrial gear) THEN write "Gear"
IF value IN (compressor; screw compressor) THEN write "Compressor"
IF value IN (gas engine) THEN write "Gas Engine"
IF value IN (diesel; HDDO; engine oil) THEN write "Diesel Engine"
IF value IN (circulating; paper machine) THEN write "Circulating"
LUB-4 iso_class
REMOVE ISO, L- and the viscosity number: ISO L-HM 46 -> HM
Allowed: HH HL HM HV HG TSA TGA CKB CKC CKD DAA DAB DAH
LUB-5 pack_size
IF value IN (drum; 55 gal drum; 205 L drum; 45 imp gal drum) THEN write "208 L"
IF value IN (5 gal pail) THEN write "18.9 L"
IF value IN (IBC; tote) THEN write "1000 L"
Standard packs first (table above), otherwise convert gallons x 3.785, quarts x 0.946
Grease
Greases are defined by consistency (NLGI), thickener and base oil viscosity. Get those three right and you can find a substitute in any warehouse.
Write the category as: Grease  You may receive: Grease; Lubricating Grease; EP Grease; Bearing Grease
Rule cards

GRS-1 nlgi_grade
Strip EP, #, grade and spaces, keep the number: EP2 -> NLGI 2; #2 -> NLGI 2
Grades 000 and 00 keep their zeros: NLGI 00

GRS-2 thickener
IF value IN (lithium; Li; lithium soap) THEN write "Lithium"
IF value IN (Li complex; Li-X; LiX; lithium complex) THEN write "Lithium Complex"
IF value IN (Ca sulphonate; calcium sulfonate; CaS) THEN write "Calcium Sulfonate"
IF value IN (polyurea; PU thickener) THEN write "Polyurea"
IF value IN (Al complex; aluminum complex) THEN write "Aluminium Complex"
IF value IN (clay; bentonite; organoclay) THEN write "Bentonite"

GRS-3 base_oil_viscosity
IF ISO VG n base THEN n cSt @ 40 °C
mm2/s and mm2/s equal cSt

GRS-4 ep_additive
IF value is EP or contains EP THEN Yes; IF non-EP THEN No

GRS-5 pack_size
Grease is sold by weight: g / 1000, lb x 0.4536, oz x 0.02835; one decimal
CHAPTER 7 · CODE FLT
Filter Element
A filter element is described by what it filters, how fine, on which basis, and with what media. Part numbers are useful but they live in the purchasing record, not here.
Write the category as: Filter Element  You may receive: Filter; Filter Element; Filter Cartridge; Cartridge; Element
Rule cards

FLT-1 filter_service
IF value IN (hydraulic; HYD) THEN write "Hydraulic"
IF value IN (LO; lube; lube oil) THEN write "Lube Oil"
IF value IN (fuel; diesel fuel) THEN write "Fuel"
IF value IN (inlet air; air intake; intake) THEN write "Air Intake"
IF value IN (coalescing; coalescer) THEN write "Coalescer"
IF value IN (gas; fuel gas) THEN write "Gas"

FLT-2 micron_rating
micron, microns, u, um, µ all become µm

FLT-3 rating_basis
IF value IN (abs; absolute; beta 200; beta 1000; B10>=200) THEN write "Absolute"
IF value IN (nom; nominal) THEN write "Nominal"

Hex Bolt
Hex bolts look simple until you meet DIN, ISO, SAE and ASTM in the same spreadsheet. The thread and the grade are the two fields people get wrong.
Write the category as: Hex Bolt  You may receive: Bolt; Hex Bolt; Hex Head Bolt; Hex Cap Screw; HHB
Rule cards
BLT-1 thread

IF metric with coarse pitch (M16 x 2.0, M12x1.75) THEN drop the pitch: M16
IF metric with fine pitch THEN keep it: M16x1.5
IF inch fraction without TPI THEN add the UNC TPI from the table on page 20: 5/8" UNC -> 5/8-11 UNC
IF inch with TPI but no series THEN assume UNC: 1/2-13 -> 1/2-13 UNC
BLT-2 length
inch x 25.4, one decimal

IF value IN (8.8; cl 8.8; class 8.8) THEN write "8.8"

IF value IN (12.9) THEN write "12.9"
IF value IN (A2 70; 304 SS 70) THEN write "A2-70"

CHAPTER 9 · CODE HSE
Hydraulic Hose
Hydraulic hose is identified by construction standard and dash size. Similar-looking standards (R2AT and 2SN) are close cousins, not twins - don't convert one into the other.
Write the category as: Hydraulic Hose  You may receive: Hose; Hydraulic Hose; Hose Assembly; Hyd Hose
Rule cards

HSE-1 hose_standard
IF value IN (R1AT; R1) THEN write "SAE 100R1AT"
IF value IN (R2AT; R2) THEN write "SAE 100R2AT"
IF value IN (1SN) THEN write "EN 853 1SN"
IF value IN (2SN) THEN write "EN 853 2SN"
IF value IN (4SP) THEN write "EN 856 4SP"
IF value IN (4SH) THEN write "EN 856 4SH"
IF value IN (R13) THEN write "SAE 100R13"

Watch out! R2AT and 2SN are not the same standard. Translate what is written; never swap one for the other.

HSE-2 dash_size
Look up inch, mm or DN in the dash-size table (page 20): 1/2 in, 12.7 mm, DN12, #8 -> -8

HSE-3 max_working_pressure
psi x 0.0689476, MPa x 10, round to whole bar

HSE-4 end_fitting
IF value IN (JIC female; JIC swivel; 37 deg female) THEN write "JIC 37° Female Swivel"
IF value IN (ORFS female; O-ring face seal) THEN write "ORFS Female Swivel"
IF value IN (BSP female; BSPP female) THEN write "BSPP Female Swivel"
IF value IN (NPT male; MNPT) THEN write "NPT Male"
IF value IN (SAE 3000 flange; code 61) THEN write "Flange Code 61"

CHAPTER 10 · CODE GLV
Safety Gloves
Gloves are PPE, so the protection levels matter as much as the size. EN 388:2016 cut levels are letters A-F; the old numeric levels can't be translated reliably.
Write the category as: Safety Gloves  You may receive: Gloves; Glove; Safety Gloves; Work Gloves; Cut Resistant Gloves
Sample field guide for testing data standardization. Keep it on your desk, not in a drawer.
Rule cards

GLV-1 glove_size
IF value IN (S; small) THEN write "7"
IF value IN (M; medium) THEN write "8"
IF value IN (L; large) THEN write "9"
IF value IN (XL) THEN write "10"
IF value IN (XXL; 2XL) THEN write "11"
IF value is 'size n' THEN n

GLV-2 cut_level
IF value is an EN 388 code like 4X43D THEN the 5th character is the cut level: Cut D
IF value is 'ISO cut C' or 'cut C' THEN Cut C
IF value is an old numeric level (level 5) or an ANSI level (A4) THEN CHECK: (no reliable conversion)

GLV-3 glove_material
IF value IN (nitrile) THEN write "Nitrile"
IF value IN (latex; natural rubber) THEN write "Latex"
IF value IN (neoprene; chloroprene) THEN write "Neoprene"
IF value IN (leather; cowhide; goatskin) THEN write "Leather"
IF value IN (Dyneema; HPPE; UHMWPE) THEN write "HPPE"
IF value IN (Kevlar; aramid; para-aramid) THEN write "Aramid"
IF value IN (PVC) THEN write "PVC"

GLV-4 coating
IF value IN (sandy nitrile; nitrile palm; foam nitrile) THEN write "Nitrile Palm"
IF value IN (PU coated palm; polyurethane palm) THEN write "PU Palm"
IF value IN (crinkle latex) THEN write "Latex Crinkle"
IF value IN (uncoated; none) THEN write "None"

GLV-5 cuff_length
inch x 25.4, round to whole mm

GLV-6 impact_protection
IF TPR back, impact, EN 388 'P' marking THEN Yes

FAQ

Q. The value is right but in the wrong field. Can I move it?
A. No (GR8). Translate what is in the row. If 'EP2' arrives in the nlgi_grade field, write NLGI 2 there; whoever sends ep_additive separately will get Yes on that row.

Q. The supplier wrote both units: '50.8 mm (2 in)'. Which do I keep?
A. The metric number only, tidied per GR4: 50.8 mm.

Q. Why 'CHECK:' and not just leaving it?
A. Because a CHECK: row is searchable. Reviewers filter on it every morning; a silently kept value is never looked at again.

Q. A brand name is the only thing I have (Viton, Kevlar, Aflas).
A. Several brand names are listed as accepted inputs and translate to the generic material. If a brand isn't listed, write CHECK: with the brand name.

Q. Is 'TBD' the same as 'CHECK:'?
A. No. TBD means nobody told us. CHECK: means somebody told us something we can't translate.

Q. Can I write 25.0 mm to show precision?
A. Not for normal fields (GR4 drops trailing zeros). O-ring dimensions are the exception: always two decimals.

Q. The category is spelled 'Oring' / 'O Ring' / 'o-ring'.
A. All the same: write O-Ring (GR1). Watch the capital R.

Q. Should I correct R2AT to 2SN because they're 'the same hose'?
A. Never. They're similar, not identical (see chapter 8).

Q. Old cut level '5' - isn't that roughly Cut D?
A. Roughly isn't good enough for PPE. Write CHECK: level 5.

Q. Two rows describe the same field for the same item with different values.
A. Translate both as they are. Duplicate detection happens later, not here.
Your end-of-batch checklist

rows.Check: [] Every Item is a category name from a chapter title, Title Case.
[] Every Attribute is a lower_snake_case field key from that chapter.
[] Picklist values match the guide exactly - capitals, spaces and symbols.
[] Numbers have one space before the unit and no trailing zeros (O-rings: two decimals).
[] No inches, psi, gallons, pounds or ounces left anywhere.
[] Missing values say TBD; untranslatable values start with CHECK: and keep the original text.
[] Row count and row order are unchanged.

Lookup tables
